messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: High GPU queue growth detected in us-west1-gpu-pool. queue_length=2148, avg_latency=4.2s, autoscaler error: "scale request denied: max_pools_reached". Pager: @Raj P oncall.

Raj P: taking it. I'm pulling logs and checking autoscaler state. Paging oncall to incident channel.

Maria L: all, FYI I can see a lot of small MIG partitions (1g.1 / 1g.2) and a handful of larger slices. Scheduler reports 37% fragmented GPU capacity that can't be used for pending requests.

Kelly S: confirmed. Queue is dominated by long-context jobs from a single route. Those are blocking continuous batching. We have ~1800 queued generator requests.

Devon H: autoscaler shows this in controller logs:
```
ERROR autoscaler.go: failed to allocate: requested_vram=24G, available_contiguous=8G, reason=fragmentation
WARN autoscaler.go: max_pools_limit reached (50). can't provision more pools
```

Raj P: looks like two problems: 1) fragmentation / MIG sizing mismatch so new pods can't find compatible slices, 2) autoscaler config has a hard cap set by reserved contract. Trying an emergency manual allocation now.

Kelly S: Raj, what's the plan? Can we evict low-priority work to free contiguous slots?

Raj P: yes. Step 1: throttle non-critical routes (route: batch-async / low-priority) and move them to a degraded fallback model. Step 2: manual pack live VMs by draining smallest MIG slices and rebinding pods to larger contiguous MIGs. Doing step 1 now.

Maria L: command for throttling (run on routing config):
```
redwoodctl routes update --name batch-async --rate-limit 5r/s --fallback-model small-fast
```
Applying.

Customer Success Bot: Alert created: CS-Ticket-8812 for customers affected by higher latency / 5xx on hosted API. Notifying top-10 users by SLA.

Devon H: while throttling takes effect, I'm going to run a manual rebalance script to consolidate allocations:
```
# prefer packing onto a smaller set of large MIG slices
node-selector: gpu.mig.size>=16g
kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data <node> --force
```
Kicking that off on 6 candidate nodes.

SRE Rotation: heads-up we're doing manual drains; load will spike on remaining nodes. I'll watch for OOMs.

Kelly S: quick check — is the reserved contract cap (max_pools) the thing blocking automated scaling? If so we should temporarily lift it for 1 hour.

Raj P: yes. On the admin console the Dedicated contract cap is 50 pools. Ops approval required. I'm requesting emergency increase now (ops pinged). If approved we'll let autoscaler create 10 more pools and parallelize placement.

Maria L: re: MIG sizing: we onboarded a mix of MIG configurations during last rollout (8g/16g slices). Some older hosts still expose 1g slices which are causing binpack gaps. Post-incident action: normalize to 8g/16g for this region.

incident-bot: Ops approval request created: OPS-INC-2201. @Kelly S tagged.

Kelly S: approved temporary increase to 60 pools for 45 minutes. Enabling.

Devon H: autoscaler accepted new pools. We see 7 new pools provisioning but placement is slow due to current fragmentation. Manual drains freed 3 large contiguous slices; scheduler started assigning 24 pending pods. Queue dropped from 2148 -> 420 in ~6m.

Raj P: customer impact summary so far: 12 customers experienced >2x latency, 4 customers saw intermittent 5xx. CS ticket updated, status page updated to "degraded". No data exfiltration risk.

Customer Success Bot: Sent "degraded" status to status.redwood.ai, email blasts queued for impacted customers.

Kelly S: thanks team. Next steps: keep throttles in place for 30m, keep extra pools for 45m, start a reclaim job to defragment cluster overnight. Assign postmortem owner.

Maria L: assigning postmortem to me. Postmortem tasks: (1) analyze MIG mix and recommend canonical sizes for us-west1, (2) autoscaler policy change: fallback to overcommit with best-effort binpack, (3) add alert for fragmentation ratio > 20%.

Raj P: handoff to oncoming oncall @SRE Rotation in 20m. I'll write up steps and runbook updates.

SRE Rotation: ack. I'll monitor queue and release extra pools when safe.

Kelly S: call out to Product & Sales: please prepare customer comms for affected enterprise accounts (copy in @Customer Success).

Devon H: quick log snippet from scheduler after rebind: 
```
INFO scheduler.go: packed 312 pods onto 12 nodes, freed 9 nodes of fragmented 1g slices
INFO queue.go: pending_count=420, avg_latency=1.1s
```
Raj P: incident declared mitigated at 2530016400. Keeping channel open for 30m for stabilization. Creating incident record INC-2530009999.

Maria L: adding one note — we should run a simulated binpack test in staging with mixed MIG sizes to catch this before rollout.

Kelly S: agreed. Great job everyone. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident INC-2530009999 created. Severity: Sev2. Postmortem owner: Maria L. Timelines logged.
